title: Tooling: exact sparse phase recipes reproduce the three frontier1042 phases pins, 12x on a shared host (no new kappa)
head: 3f21415bd54bfc7028c3d92f047cac876bc95a91
body:
**Tooling (verification engineering). No new κ. No pinned file changes, and no check is weakened.**

## What

A cold `make frontier1094-verify` runs `verify_frontier1042.py` as its `baseline1042-cold` stage. That replay calls the pinned serial `phases_full.py` three times, in the cells, chain and slots stages. In the maintainer's recorded run these three steps take **469 s of 1162 s** (199.4 + 134.4 + 135.3). #1151 parallelised the five layer-end-control steps and states that it does not re-measure these three.

Two merged exact fast paths already exist: Ali Romman's sparse compiler (#1029, `research/selected-replay-fastpath/`) and thakrarsagar's parallel runner (#1041, `research/phase-recipes-parallel/`). Both were measured only on the PR942 U8 word. `research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/` checks them on the three k8 words of the selected chain.

## Result

The three canonical words come from `research/community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz`. Their decompressed digests equal the `canonical_sha256` in LEAVER-PINS-k8, CHAIN-PINS-k8 and SLOT-PINS-k8. For each word:

- **Recipes.** `selected-replay-fastpath/run.py --engine sparse` writes a `CLIFFORD-RECIPES.json` that is **byte-identical** to the archived maintainer recipes. Its digest is the pinned `clifford_recipes_sha256`: cells `aab63b0a…`, chain `e3bfdfa2…`, slots `d0768f21…`.
- **Review.** Every `CLIFFORD-REVIEW.json` field except `seconds` equals the archived review.
- **Other engines.** The dense PR662 evaluator and `phases_parallel.py --engine dense662` reproduce the same bytes.

Same-host timings, macOS arm64, 10 cores, Python 3.14.7. The host was shared, with load average 10–29. The receipt is `BENCHMARK-macos-arm64.json`.

| Command | cells | chain | slots | Total wall (CPU) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| maintainer recording, pinned serial (other host) | 199.4 | 134.4 | 135.3 | 469.1 |
| pinned serial `phases_full.py` via `run_portable.py` | 80.3 | 82.4 | 88.2 | 250.8 (250) |
| `run.py --engine dense` (PR662) | 11.7 | 14.2 | 13.8 | 39.8 (39) |
| `run.py --engine sparse` (PR1029) | 7.9 | 7.8 | 5.0 | 20.7 (19) |
| `phases_parallel.py --jobs 10 --engine dense662` (PR1041) | 2.8 | 2.9 | 3.1 | 8.8 (70) |

All times are in seconds. On this host the sparse compiler is 12× faster than the pinned serial step in wall time, and uses one core. The parallel dense runner is 29× faster but uses about 10 cores.

## Controls

`verify.py` runs two controls on a corrupted cells word. Neither may reproduce the pin.

- **C1.** One one-dimensional frame is changed to a different line. It must be rejected by an `AssertionError`, with no recipes written.
- **C2.** One edge is redirected to a frame of a different dimension. It must compile, but to different recipes.

Both behaviours are asserted exactly.

A bit flip inside a *full-rank* frame keeps the span, so it is not a corruption. My first draft control did this and was replaced. `-O` is refused. #1029's package keeps its own controls, proof and gate tests, and this PR does not repeat them.

## Wiring (maintainers' call, not done here)

Later stages consume these outputs. `verify_slots.py` asserts both recipe digests, and `verify_t16.py` copies both CLIFFORD files forward and binds them.

- **cells.** `reproduce_leaver.py --skip-phases` works with an external `run.py` call and pin assertion.
- **chain.** `reproduce_leaver_chain.py --skip-phases` **fails**: it ends with `assert got == pins` over the whole CHAIN-PINS dictionary.
- **slots.** `verify_slots.py` has no switch.
- The T16 provider binder asserts the review's status, digests, global-phase flag and adapter count. The fast-path review matches on all of them, and `verify.py` checks this.
- All these scripts are manifest-pinned. The serial path stays the reference.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/verify.py              # ~20 s; PASS_FRONTIER1042_PHASE_FASTPATH
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath --check-only
python3 -B research/frontier1042-phase-fastpath/bench.py NEW_DIR sparse,dense,par-dense662,pinned   # ~6 min
```

The package uses only the standard library. `verify.py` passed on Python 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14, and the registered package check passes.

## Scope and limits

- The recipes are compiled from the **archived** words, which the canonical pins bind. A cold rebuild that reproduces those pins feeds the lowering identical input.
- Scalar-interface integration and the global emitted program are unchanged obligations.
- The host was shared during the timings (load average 15–23), so the numbers are descriptive only.

1. Should the cold replay use the sparse compiler for these three steps? Scaling the measured 12× ratio, it would save about 430 s on the recorded machine, and with #1151 the frontier1042 run would drop to roughly 300 s.
2. Do other archived replays spend comparable time in the 23 byte-identical `phases_full.py` copies?
